Subject: Warm pass: Meridian Health implementation canvas & technical asks

Team —

Quick warm pass for Meridian Health (attached MAP + SOW draft). They signed the agreement yesterday and will be our first east-coast deployment on the dedicated capacity tier. Key context up-front:

- Contract: MSA signed, SOW still in draft (see attached). Procurement expects final SOW + invoice terms next week.
- Go-live target: internal target 2028-09-15 (customer wants pilot in prod for a 30-day validation window).
- Initial workload: two inference routes (chat + document-embedding) with expected peak of ~600 rps tokens and steady-state ~40 rps.
- Data residency: US-only (no cross-region replication).
- Security: they requested SOC 2 evidence and encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS. Procurement already asked for a short inventory; I attached the SOC checklist they asked for.

Customer technical contacts:
  - Sylvia Mendez (Dir, Clinical AI) — sylvia.mendez@meridianhealth.org
  - Jonathan Park (Cloud Architect) — jonathan.park@meridianhealth.org

Asks for CS/Implementation:
  1) Owner nomination — who will be primary STC (steward) for Meridian? They want a single point of contact for scheduling deep technical calls.
  2) Initial runbook — we should share a short preflight checklist (network/whitelisting, KMS handshake, model variant + quantization plan).
  3) Capacity planning — propose an initial Dedicated reservation profile and burst plan (they're sensitive to latency spikes in clinical workflows).
  4) Acceptance criteria — define what success looks like for the 30-day pilot (latency p95, error rates, and sample prompt set pass rates).

Attachments: Meridian-MAP-v1.pdf (mutual action plan), SOW-draft-Redwood-vMeridian.docx

I'll be available to join kickoff and procurement synces next week (Mon/Tue mornings PT).

Thanks —
David

Thanks David — good context. A few clarifying Qs before we nominate the steward: 

1) Is the commitment for dedicated GPUs per-month or do they want an initial trial reservation with an option to convert? That changes the financial ops we propose.
2) For KMS, do they require HSM-backed keys or a managed KMS is fine? Sylvia mentioned \"customer-managed KMS\" in our call but we should confirm HSM requirement.
3) Do they plan to use streaming responses in the clinical UI or synchronous short responses? This affects the batching and batching windows we'll suggest.

Irene — can you take a look at the attached MAP and flag anything that looks like a likely blocker for our standard onboarding playbook? Looking for network/IP ranges, required ports, and any unsupported model features called out (e.g., function-calling hooks to be used server-side vs client-side).

If no major blockers, I can nominate Marissa as the primary steward (she's available for a July kickoff) and propose a 2-week SOW turnaround for procurement redlines.

-Karthik
VP, Customer Success Operations

Hi David & team —

Thanks for the concise summary. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement would like the SOW to explicitly call out data retention (30 days for transient logs, 365 days for usage metrics) and an initial billable forecast for the pilot. Can Redwood provide a pilot estimate we can include in the SOW?
- KMS: we will be using our Azure Key Vault (customer-managed KMS). Not HSM at this time.
- Streaming: our primary UX will use streaming for clinician prompts (low-latency), with a fallback short-response synchronous path for smaller events. Latency p95 target is <= 180ms for chat in the primary region.

Jonathan will be the technical lead for scheduling infra/network work — Jonathan, can you share your preferred time windows next week for a 60-minute tech deep-dive?

All — thanks for the context. I reviewed the MAP and SOW draft and noted the following operational items (high-level):

- Network/Firewall: Meridian will need three IP ranges whitelisted for our Dedicated pool and a scheduled change window (we prefer a 2-hour block).
- KMS: Azure Key Vault integration is supported; we'll need a service principal + read-only access to the key metadata and a short HLD for key rotation responsibilities. No HSM necessary.
- Streaming + Batching: for the streaming path we'll configure a small continuous-batch window (20ms) and a separate low-latency lane. Expect additional cost for the low-latency lane; I'll attach a cost delta in the follow-up.
- Acceptance criteria (proposed): 
    * Latency: p95 chat <= 180ms in the primary region under expected load.
    * Error rate: < 0.5% request failures.
    * Functionality: 95% of 50-sample prompts in the clinical prompt set must pass the evaluation suite.

Owner & next steps:
  - Primary steward: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.ai) — will be the day-to-day CS contact and runbook owner.
  - Implementation lead (infra & config): Irene Choi (irene_choi@redwood.ai) — I will schedule the tech deep-dive with Jonathan next week.

I'll add the small cost delta and a short preflight checklist to the Drive doc and share the link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3C4D

David — can you confirm procurement's preferred invoicing cadence (monthly vs milestone) so we can align the SOW language?

Cheers —
Irene Choi
Senior Implementation Manager | Redwood Inference
